data.narrative:
NVision Imaging Technologies is a Series A biotech company that has raised $20M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comparable universe of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-sector peers including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Stage-progression analysis, the primary applicable method, uses the $20M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to next-stage rounds, yielding $40M. Peer-median triangulation could not be applied; while 8 same-sector private peers exist, none of the narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, similar valuation tier) produced the minimum 3 datapoints required for statistical credibility. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple—the sector median stands at 5.6x across the three public tickers—cannot be executed absent NVision's revenue disclosure, which is standard for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $34M to $46M, with $40M as the median. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single method. The primary uncertainty is the absence of disclosed revenue, which would unlock public-multiple anchoring and potentially tighten the estimate. A secondary uncertainty is sparse private-peer financial data at the Series A stage in this subsector.
